# docs/memory/release/

<!-- Generated by php tools/memory_index.php from the frontmatter of each file, except the key rules between the two marker lines, which are written by hand. -->

Versions, migrations and upgrade steps, change log rules, release status.

## Key rules

<!-- key-rules:start -->
- Add a schema change as a sub-step of the open version with the idempotent `install_*` helpers; never open a new version number while one is open (`how-to-add-migration.md`).
- List every new table in `get_tables()` (`install/index.php`), or a reinstall keeps the old table and the site silently runs on the old schema (`how-to-add-migration.md`).
- Probe by exact name (`pg_schema_has()`, `WHERE Field =`), never `SHOW ... LIKE`: `_` is a wildcard and the wrong column counts as present (`schema-probe-rules.md`).
- Keep login, the install lock and `initialize_user()` working on the previous released schema: files land before the upgrade runs (`upgrade-bridge-rule.md`).
- Run a new step twice on a dev DB; a DB that already ran the open version needs `config.version` set back to 2026.4.10 first (`rerun-upgrade-steps.md`).
- Never change what a released version's migration brings, its `versions.php` row or its changelog heading; only its body may be fixed for sites that have not run it (`released-vs-open-version.md`).
- Take a step label from the open version's call list on `origin/development` and from open PRs, never from notes; labels are names, the call order runs (`version-numbering.md`).
- Compare versions with `version_compare()`, never `<`, `strcmp()` or `sort()`: as strings 2026.11.0 sorts before 2026.4.10 (`version-numbering.md`).
- Give a step that may outrun 60-90 s a pause (`install_pause()`) or hand its data work to the general job with a cursor in config (`migration-long-steps.md`).
<!-- key-rules:end -->

## Files

- database-server-compatibility.md: Which MySQL and MariaDB versions the install and the upgrade steps run on, why MySQL 5.6 and MariaDB 10.1 are refused, the 2022.2 DROP DEFAULT failure (issue #464) and how to test a server.
- how-to-add-migration.md: Checklist for a DB schema change: open-version sub-step or new number, file template, install_note(), heavy tables, get_tables() for a new table, changelog, step label, rules, finishing checks.
- migration-long-steps.md: How an upgrade step that may outrun the web server's time limit is written: restart-safe work, the 30 s pass budget and install_pause(), backfills with a cursor in config, schema apart from data.
- migration-step-helpers.md: How to write an upgrade step with the runner.php install_* helpers: check-then-act, exact-name probes, re-runnable data statements, enum-narrowing MODIFY.
- migration-system-layout.md: Where DB schema changes live (includes/migrations files and roles) and how version entry functions and sub-steps are named. Direct SQL for schema is forbidden.
- release-status.md: Last released version (2026.4.10), the open version (2026.11.0, first calendar-versioned number), its migration file and step labels, how a release branch, tag and GitHub release are made
- released-vs-open-version.md: Released versions are closed, unreleased ones open: where the status is recorded, how the upgrade loop compares versions, no new number while one is open.
- rerun-upgrade-steps.md: How to re-run an open version's upgrade steps on a dev DB (config.version rollback by SQL or the Yazılımı Onar card, which versions it offers) and the package repair card.
- schema-probe-rules.md: Code that reads a table/column added by a migration probes first with pg_schema_has() (cache file, invalidation, pg_schema_forget() for a recheck); which hot probes use it, the router's config check
- stale-migration-file-protection.md: Why a stale migration file survived a zip upload (0555 folders) and the protection layers: permission scan, update screen, status card, repair, extraction.
- upgrade-automation-and-testing.md: Cron/automated upgrade entry points (AUTOMATED_UPGRADE_SECRET), admin-session behavior, and where the upgrade system test protocol lives.
- upgrade-bridge-rule.md: Upgrade bridge rule: code lands before the schema, so login, install lock and initialize_user() must run on the previous schema; gate and mandatory test.
- upgrade-changelog-rules.md: changelog.txt format (English, only plan-driven major features as [NEW], one [FIX]/[SECURITY]/[SCHEME] line per version); the detail goes to docs/memory.
- upgrade-runner-behavior.md: How the upgrade runner reacts to failing statements, locks and fatals, and how the install screen runs one version per request, with heavy-table preflight.
- version-numbering.md: Version numbers from 2026.11.0 on are year.month.patch (calendar versioning): what each part means, which number an open version takes, why three parts and no leading zero, step labels.
